Gravity pulls inward while fusion heat pushes outward. These two forces balance perfectly, keeping the star steady for a long time!

Hinihila ng gravity papasok habang ang init ng fusion ay nagtutulak palabas. Magkapatas ang dalawang puwersa, kaya panatag ang bituin sa mahabang panahon!

Why is it harder to make static in the Philippines?

Our air is often humid! Moisture in the air carries the charge away before it builds up. You'll only feel static easily on dry days or in air-conditioned rooms.

Bakit mas mahirap gumawa ng static sa Pilipinas?

Kasi madalas mahalumigmig ang hangin natin! Ang moisture sa hangin ay nagdadala ng charge bago pa ito mag-ipon. Mas madali kang makakaramdam ng static sa tuyong araw o sa naka-aircon na room.
copy.bis:

Kay kasagaran umog ang atong hangin! Ang moisture sa hangin modala sa charge palayo sa dili pa matigom. Mas sayon nimo mabati ang static sa uga nga adlaw o sa naay aircon nga kwarto.

Kapag bukas ang screen, nagkakaroon ito ng static charge! Hinahila nito ang maliliit na alikabok mula sa hangin, at dumidikit ang mga ito sa screen.

Synthetic fabrics like nylon and polyester build up static charge faster than cotton, making them cling to you because of static!

Why is static electricity stronger and more common in dry air?

In dry, cold, or low-humidity air, static electricity is stronger! In damp or humid air, the charge leaks away easily, making sparks rarer.

Kapag tuyo o kulang sa halumigmig ang hangin, mas malakas ang static electricity! Sa basa o mahalumigmig na hangin, mabilis nawawala ang charge kaya bihira ang spark.

Ang Faraday cage ay isang lalagyan o balot na gawa sa metal na nagharang ng mga electric field sa loob nito! Ang mga saradong metal na sasakyan at microwave oven ay gumaganap bilang Faraday cage para sa iba't ibang layunin.

Lightning starts with a stepped leader! It's an invisible path of ionized air stepping down from a cloud before a return stroke shoots up to create the flash!

Nagsisimula ang kidlat sa stepped leader! Ito'y di-nakikitang daan ng ionized na hangin pababa mula sa ulap bago ang return stroke pataas para sa flash!
copy.bis:

Steel is a special alloy made by mixing iron with just a small amount of carbon!

Ang steel ay isang alloy na gawa sa paghahalo ng bakal (iron) at kaunting carbon!

copy.en: Your stomach and brain send signals to each other, so your body knows whether you're still hungry or already full.
copy.tl: Nag-uusap ang tiyan at utak natin sa pamamagitan ng mga senyales, kaya nalalaman natin kung gutom pa tayo o busog na.
copy.bis: Ang atong tiyan ug utok nagpadalag mga senyales sa usag-usa, mao nga mahibaloan nato kung gigutom pa kita o busog na.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a tsunami is caused by an earthquake or movement under the sea
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a tsunami is caused by an earthquake, which is necessary background, but it does not explain how earthquakes generate tsunamis or how they devastate shoreline communities as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a typhoon as the cause of a storm surge, which is a weather disturbance, but it does not describe effects of weather disturbances in or near the Philippines. The contrast with tsunami is not instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: A storm surge is caused by a typhoon, while a tsunami is caused by an earthquake or movement under the sea!
copy.tl: Ang storm surge ay dulot ng bagyo, samantalang ang tsunami ay dulot ng lindol o paggalaw sa ilalim ng dagat!
copy.bis: Ang storm surge tungod sa bagyo, samtang ang tsunami tungod sa linog o paglihok ilawom sa dagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: storms can raise the water level even more
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses storms raising water levels and causing coastal flooding, which is tangentially related to typhoons but does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. It provides no direct instructional support for either part of the competency.

copy.en: Spring tides are higher than normal, and storms can raise the water level even more through increased rainfall and winds, causing coastal flooding.
copy.tl: Mas mataas kaysa normal ang spring tides, at maaaring mas lalo pang itaas ng bagyo ang lebel ng tubig dahil sa dagdag na ulan at hangin, na nagdudulot ng pagbaha sa mga baybayin.
copy.bis: Ang spring tides mas taas kaysa normal, ug ang bagyo makapataas pa gyud sa lebel sa tubig pinaagi sa dugang nga ulan ug hangin, nga nagpahinabo sa pagbaha sa mga baybayon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helping CFC chemicals destroy ozone much faster every spring
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helping CFC chemicals destroy ozone much faster every spring
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a factor (cold polar stratospheric clouds) that speeds up a chemical reaction (ozone destruction), which touches on factors affecting reaction rates. copy.en: The ozone hole is biggest over Antarctica! It is so cold there that special clouds form, helping CFC chemicals destroy ozone much faster every spring.
copy.tl: Pinakamalaki ang butas ng ozone sa ibabaw ng Antarctica! Sobrang lamig doon kaya may natatanging ulap na tumutulong sa CFC para mas mabilis sirain ang ozone tuwing tagsibol.
copy.bis: Pinakadako ang lungag sa ozone ibabaw sa Antarctica! Hilabihan ang katugnaw didto kaya naay pinasahing panganod nga mutabang sa CFC aron mas paspas maguba ang ozone matag tagsibol.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer is healing because we banned CFCs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ozone layer recovery from CFCs, which is an atmospheric topic, but it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. No direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer is healing because we banned CFCs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a global environmental issue addressed by banning CFCs, but the competency focuses on local community issues and concerns addressed by science, such as waste treatment. The ozone layer is not a local community concern, so this is only broadly related.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: full recovery will take several more decades
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions recovery of the ozone layer, which is tangentially related to environmental change, but it does not identify local impacts of global climate change or suggest individual actions to reduce global warming. No direct support for the competency.

copy.en: The ozone layer is healing because we banned CFCs! But old chemicals stay in the air a long time, so full recovery will take several more decades.
copy.tl: Gumagaling na ang ozone layer dahil bawal na ang CFCs! Pero matagal pa mananatili ang lumang kemikal, kaya ilang dekada pa bago lubos na gumaling.
copy.bis: Nagaayo na ang ozone layer kay gidili na ang CFCs! Pero dugay pa magpabilin ang daang kemikal, so pipila pa ka dekada antes mahingpit ang pag-ayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer is super important, but it's actually very thin!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the ozone layer is thin; it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere, such as absorption of ultraviolet radiation. The shared topic of atmosphere/Sun is not enough for direct support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer is super important, but it's actually very thin!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the ozone layer's importance but gives no safety measures to avoid harmful effects of the Sun's light. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The ozone layer is super important, but it's actually very thin! If you squished all the ozone together, it would be thinner than two stacked coins.
copy.tl: Sobrang importante ng ozone layer, pero napakamanipis talaga niya! Kung titipunin mo lahat ng ozone, mas manipis pa ito kaysa sa dalawang magkapatong na barya.
copy.bis: Importante kaayo ang ozone layer, apan nipis kaayo gyud niini! Kon tigumon nimo ang tanang ozone, mas nipis pa kini kay sa duha ka gipatong nga sinsilyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: light refracts as it passes from water into air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes refraction with an everyday example (straw in water), but the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection and refraction using specific equipment (plane/curved mirrors, transparent blocks, lenses, prisms). copy.en: When you put a straw in a glass of water, it looks bent at the surface! This happens because light refracts as it passes from water into air.
copy.tl: Kapag inilagay ang dayami sa baso ng tubig, mukhang nakabiko ito sa ibabaw! Nangyayari ito dahil sa refraction ng liwanag mula tubig papuntang hangin.
copy.bis: Kung ibutang ang dayami sa baso sa tubig, murag nakabiko kini sa ibabaw! Mahitabo kini tungod sa refraction sa suga gikan sa tubig ngadto sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A stress fracture is a tiny crack in a bone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific bone injury (stress fracture) but does not describe how the skeletal system works, nor any other body system. It only mentions bone, which is part of the skeletal system, but provides no functional description of the system.

copy.en:
What is a stress fracture?

A stress fracture is a tiny crack in a bone, caused by using it too much again and again — like running too much.
copy.tl:
Ano ang stress fracture?

Ang stress fracture ay maliit na lamat sa buto, dulot ng paulit-ulit na sobrang paggamit — tulad ng sobrang pagtakbo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang stress fracture?

Ang stress fracture kay gamay nga liki sa bukog, tungod sa balik-balik nga sobra nga paggamit — sama sa sobra nga pagdagan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A string's pitch depends on three things!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains factors affecting the pitch of a string (length, tension, thickness). The competency G3-F-4 requires exploring and describing how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as a ringing bell or hearing noises. Pitch variation is a property of sound, but the card does not address how sound is produced or transmitted, so it only shares the broad subject of sound.

copy.en:
What changes a string's pitch?

A string's pitch depends on three things! Shorter length means higher pitch, tighter tension means higher pitch, and thinner thickness also means a higher pitch!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagbabago sa pitch ng string?

Ang pitch ng string ay nakadepende sa tatlong bagay! Mas maikling haba ay mas mataas ang pitch, mas mahigpit na tensyon ay mas mataas, at mas manipis ay mas mataas!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagbag-o sa pitch sa string?

Ang pitch sa string nagdepende sa tulo ka butang! Mas mubo nga gitas-on mas taas ang pitch, mas guyod nga tensyon mas taas, ug mas nipis nga kapal mas taas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keeping everything in compression
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how a dome distributes weight and stays in compression, but it does not address how forces change the shape of objects (pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, squeezed). The concept of compression is related to forces but does not directly support the competency's focus on shape change.

copy.en:
How can a dome hold up a huge heavy roof?

A dome is an arch spun in 3D! Weight spreads in every direction down to the base, keeping everything in compression.
copy.tl:
Paano kaya kayang buhatin ng dome ang napakalaking bubong?

Ang dome ay arko na pinaikot sa 3D! Ang bigat ay kumakalat sa lahat ng direksyon pababa, kaya lahat ay nasa compression.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdala sa dome sa dako nga atop?

Ang dome usa ka arko nga giputol sa 3D! Ang gibug-aton nagkatibulaag sa tanang direksyon paubos, nagpabilin sa compression.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: styrofoam is a great heat insulator

It only states a general property of styrofoam without linking it to the competency's required concepts.

copy.en: Styrofoam containers keep your food hot or cold for a long time because styrofoam is a great heat insulator!
copy.tl: Ang styrofoam na lalagyan ay nagpapanatiling mainit o malamig ang pagkain dahil mahusay itong insulador ng init!
copy.bis: Ang styrofoam nga sudlanan nagpabilin nga init o bugnaw ang pagkaon kay maayo kini nga insulador sa init!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One plate slides beneath another in a process called subduction, forming deep ocean trenches!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that subduction occurs and forms trenches. It does not explain how subduction impacts the plate above it, which is the core of G10-E-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One plate slides beneath another in a process called subduction, forming deep ocean trenches!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions one plate-boundary process (subduction) but does not describe the structures, movements, and events at each type of plate boundary as required by G10-E-2.

copy.en:
What happens to tectonic plates around the Philippines?

One plate slides beneath another in a process called subduction, forming deep ocean trenches!
copy.tl:
Anong nangyayari sa mga plaka sa palibot ng Pilipinas?

Lumulubog ang isang plaka sa ilalim ng isa pa sa proseso na tinatawag na subduction, na lumilikha ng malalalim na kanal sa karagatan!
copy.bis:
Unsay nahitabo sa mga plaka palibot sa Pilipinas?

Ang usa ka plaka molubog ilalom sa lain pinaagi sa proseso nga gitawag og subduction, nga naghimo og lawom nga mga kanal sa dagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sublimation turns solid straight into gas, while deposition turns gas right back into solid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The competency specifically requires describing melting, evaporation, freezing, and condensation using diagrams/flowcharts. The card teaches sublimation and deposition, which are not among the listed processes, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sublimation turns solid straight into gas, while deposition turns gas right back into solid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on temperature-driven changes such as solid to liquid to gas. Sublimation and deposition are state changes but are not the examples given and are not described in terms of temperature change, so the card only shares the broad topic of state changes.

copy.en: Sublimation and deposition are total opposites! Sublimation turns solid straight into gas, while deposition turns gas right back into solid.
copy.tl: Ang sublimation at deposition ay magkasalungat! Ang sublimation ay solido tungo sa gas, at ang deposition ay gas tungo sa solido.
copy.bis: Ang sublimation ug deposition magsukwahi! Ang sublimation solido ngadto sa gas, ug ang deposition gas ngadto sa solido.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it goes straight from solid to gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sublimation (solid to gas), but G6-M-1 specifically lists melting, evaporation, freezing, and condensation, and requires diagrams/flowcharts. Sublimation is not among the listed processes, and the card uses no diagram or flowchart.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it goes straight from solid to gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a change of state (solid to gas) but attributes it to normal air pressure, not to a change in temperature. G5-M-6 focuses on temperature-driven state changes such as solid to liquid to gas. The card does not directly support the temperature-change concept.

copy.en: At Earth's normal air pressure, carbon dioxide can't stay liquid—it goes straight from solid to gas!
copy.tl: Sa normal na presyon ng hangin sa Earth, hindi maaaring maging likido ang carbon dioxide kaya dumidiretso ito sa gas!
copy.bis: Sa normal nga presyon sa hangin sa kalibutan, dili mahimong likido ang carbon dioxide mao nga diretso kini ngadto sa gas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A submarine sinks by filling its ballast tanks with water, and floats by replacing that water with air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water (liquid) and air (gas) but does not teach the three states of matter or their identification. The focus is on buoyancy and ballast, not on states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A submarine sinks by filling its ballast tanks with water, and floats by replacing that water with air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address mass or volume/space. It explains sinking and floating via ballast tanks, which is a density/buoyancy concept, not a direct lesson on matter having mass and taking up space.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A submarine sinks by filling its ballast tanks with water, and floats by replacing that water with air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sinking and floating but does not explicitly describe the effects of gravity on motion. Gravity is implied in sinking/floating, but the card does not teach or observe gravity's effect on an object's motion.

copy.en:
How does a submarine sink and float?

A submarine sinks by filling its ballast tanks with water, and floats by replacing that water with air!
copy.tl:
Paano lumulubog at lumulutang ang submarino?

Lumulubog ang submarino kapag pinupuno ng tubig ang ballast tanks, at lumulutang kapag pinapalitan ng hangin ang tubig!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglubog ug paglutaw sa submarino?

Mounlod ang submarino kon pun-on og tubig ang ballast tanks, ug molutaw kon ilisan og hangin ang tubig!

What is the scientific name for the table sugar you use every day?

The scientific name of table sugar is sucrose! Sweet and simple!
copy.tl:
Ano ang siyentipikong pangalan ng table sugar na ginagamit mo araw-araw?

Ang siyentipikong pangalan ng table sugar ay sucrose (sukrosa)! Matamis at simple!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang siyentipikong ngalan sa table sugar nga imong gigamit matag adlaw?

Ang siyentipikong ngalan sa table sugar kay sucrose (sukrosa)! Tam-is ug simple!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: From sugarcane, a sweet, tall grass widely grown in the Philippines!

assignedReviews.reason: The card names sugarcane as a plant but does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat, and no particular habitat is identified. The format-required activity is not supported.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies sugarcane as a plant but does not describe the difference between living and non-living things or give contrasting examples. It only touches on a living thing without teaching the competency.

copy.en:
Where does most of our sugar come from?

From sugarcane, a sweet, tall grass widely grown in the Philippines!
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang karamihan ng asukal natin?

Sa tubo, isang matamis na halamang malaki at malawak itanim sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis:
Asa naggikan ang kadaghanan sa atong asukal?

Sa tubó, usa ka tam-is nga taas nga tanom nga gitanom sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it gives your body awesome energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions energy for the body but does not describe any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) or how they work. It is only tangentially related to nutrition/energy.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies sucrose as a carbohydrate and mentions energy, but does not describe photosynthesis or respiration, nor their raw materials and products. It is background knowledge about a respiratory substrate, not direct instruction on the competency.

copy.en: Table sugar is a carbohydrate called sucrose, and it gives your body awesome energy!
copy.tl: Ang table sugar ay isang carbohydrate na tinatawag na sucrose, na nagbibigay ng enerhiya sa katawan!
copy.bis: Ang asukal sa lamesa usa ka carbohydrate nga gitawag og sucrose, ug naghatag kini og kusog sa lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It goes through physical changes! It starts as liquid juice, becomes thick syrup, and finally turns into solid sugar crystals.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sugar changing from liquid to syrup to solid, but does not name the specific state-change processes (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) and does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It goes through physical changes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'physical changes' but does not explain why physical changes are reversible or why chemical changes are irreversible. It only labels the sugar transformation as physical without addressing reversibility.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It starts as liquid juice, becomes thick syrup, and finally turns into solid sugar crystals.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a change from liquid to solid but does not describe how temperature causes the change of state, nor does it use the specific state-change vocabulary (solid to liquid to gas) expected at this grade.

copy.en:
How does sugar change form when we make it?

It goes through physical changes! It starts as liquid juice, becomes thick syrup, and finally turns into solid sugar crystals.
copy.tl:
Paano nagbabago ang anyo ng asukal habang ginagawa?

Dumaan ito sa physical changes! Nagsisimula bilang likidong katas, nagiging malapot na arnibal, at nagiging solid sugar crystals.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagbag-o ang porma sa asukal samtang gihimo?

Moagi kini sa physical changes! Nagsugod isip likido nga duga, nahimong baga nga arnibal, ug nagiging solid sugar crystals.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: make your blood sugar shoot up very quickly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions blood sugar (glucose level), which is one indicator of homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor explain maintenance or indicators. assignedReviews.card_evidence: make your blood sugar shoot up very quickly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify or describe any parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or how they work. Blood sugar response is not digestive system anatomy or function as specified by the competency.

copy.en: Sugary drinks like soft drinks make your blood sugar shoot up very quickly.
copy.tl: Ang matatamis na inumin tulad ng softdrinks ay mabilis na nagpapataas ng asukal sa dugo.
copy.bis: Ang tam-is nga mga ilimnon sama sa softdrinks paspas nga magpataas sa asukal sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How many types of elements are in sulfur trioxide (SO₃)?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies that SO₃ contains two elements (sulfur and oxygen), which touches on the idea that compounds are made of elements. It only gives a basic elemental composition fact, which is related background but not direct instruction for this competency.

copy.en:
How many types of elements are in sulfur trioxide, SO₃?

Sulfur trioxide contains two types of elements: sulfur and oxygen. The formula SO₃ shows one sulfur atom and three oxygen atoms.
copy.tl:
Ilang uri ng element ang nasa sulfur trioxide, SO₃?

Ang sulfur trioxide ay naglalaman ng dalawang uri ng element: sulfur at oxygen. Ipinapakita ng formula na SO₃ ang isang sulfur atom at tatlong oxygen atom.
copy.bis:
Pila ka klase sa element ang naa sa sulfur trioxide, SO₃?

Ang sulfur trioxide adunay duha ka klase sa element: sulfur ug oxygen. Ang formula nga SO₃ nagpakita og usa ka sulfur atom ug tulo ka oxygen atom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's magnetic force guides the Sun's particles toward the poles!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun's particles but does not describe the Sun's composition, size, or main radiated energy. It is about auroras and Earth's magnetic field, not the Sun's overall characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Auroras are seen only near Earth's two poles, not in tropical places like the Philippines.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses auroras and the Sun's particles, not observing or describing natural objects commonly seen in the sky such as the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. It does not support the guided observation/description skill.

copy.en: Auroras are seen only near Earth's two poles, not in tropical places like the Philippines. Earth's magnetic force guides the Sun's particles toward the poles!
copy.tl: Nakikita lang ang aurora malapit sa magkabilang poste ng Mundo, hindi sa tropikal na lugar tulad ng Pilipinas. Ginagabayan ng magnetikong puwersa ng Mundo ang mga particle ng Araw patungo sa mga poste!
copy.bis: Makita lang ang aurora duol sa duha ka poste sa Kalibutan, dili sa tropikal nga dapit sama sa Pilipinas. Gogiya sa magnetikong puwersa sa Kalibutan ang mga particle sa Adlaw padulong sa mga poste!

copy.en:
Does the Sun spin the same everywhere?

Nope! The Sun's equator rotates faster — about 25 days per spin — while its poles take about 35 days. This differential rotation twists the Sun's magnetic field and helps produce sunspots.
copy.tl:
Pareho ba ang pag-ikot ng Araw?

Hindi! Ang equator ng Araw umiikot nang mas mabilis — 25 araw — habang ang poles 35 araw. Ang differential rotation na ito ay nagpi-twist sa magnetic field ng Araw at lumilikha ng sunspots.
copy.bis:
Pareho ba ang pagkibot sa Adlaw?

Dili! Ang equator sa Adlaw nagkibot nga mas paspas — 25 ka adlaw — samtang ang pole 35 ka adlaw. Kining differential rotation nagpi-twist sa magnetic field sa Adlaw ug nagtabang paghimo og sunspots.

copy.en: Earth's orbit is an ellipse, so our distance from the Sun changes! We are closest in January (perihelion) at 147 million km, and farthest in July (aphelion) at 152 million km!
copy.tl: Ang orbit ng Earth ay ellipse, kaya nagbabago ang distansya natin sa Araw! Pinakamalapit tayo sa Enero (perihelion) sa 147 million km, at pinakamalayo sa Hulyo (aphelion) sa 152 million km!
copy.bis: Ang orbit sa Yuta usa ka ellipse, mao nga nagbag-o ang distansya nato sa Adlaw! Pinakaduol ta sa Enero (perihelion) sa 147 million km, ug pinakalayo sa Hulyo (aphelion) sa 152 million km!

copy.en:
How many Earths can fit inside the Sun?

A lot! About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the giant Sun.
copy.tl:
Ilang Mundo ang kasya sa loob ng Araw?

Napakarami! Mga 1.3 milyong Mundo ang kasya sa loob ng napakalaking Araw.
copy.bis:
Pila ka Yuta ang mahaom sa sulod sa Adlaw?

Daghan kaayo! Mga 1.3 ka milyon ka Yuta ang mahaom sa sulod sa dako nga Adlaw.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition

It only touches on the solar system boundary, so it does not directly support describing the solar system's structure, major objects, features, or composition.

copy.en: The heliosphere is a giant bubble of solar wind made by the Sun. Its edge, the heliopause, marks the boundary of our solar system—and Voyager 1 crossed it in 2012!
copy.tl: Ang heliosphere ay isang malaking bula ng solar wind mula sa Araw. Ang heliopause ang hangganan ng solar system—at lumampas dito ang Voyager 1 noong 2012!
copy.bis: Ang heliosphere usa ka dako nga bula sa solar wind gikan sa Adlaw. Ang heliopause mao ang tumoy sa solar system—ug mitabok niini ang Voyager 1 niadtong 2012!

copy.en:
How long does the Sun's light take to reach Earth?

Even traveling super fast, sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach us! When you look at the Sun, you're actually seeing it from 8 minutes ago.
copy.tl:
Ilang minuto bago dumating ang liwanag ng Araw sa Mundo?

Kahit napakabilis, tumatagal ng mga 8 minuto ang liwanag ng Araw bago dumating! Kapag tumingin ka, nakikita mo ang itsura nito 8 minuto na ang nakalipas.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay ang kahayag sa Adlaw nga moabot sa Kalibutan?

Bisan kusog kaayo molupad, moabot sa mga 8 ka minuto ang kahayag sa Adlaw! Kung motan-aw ka, imong nakita ang dagway niini 8 ka minuto na ang milabay.

copy.tl: Mainit buong taon sa Pilipinas dahil mataas ang araw sa langit at malakas ang sikat nito!
copy.bis: Init tibuok tuig sa Pilipinas tungod kay taas ang adlaw sa langit ug kusog ang sidlak niini!

copy.en: For every degree of latitude you travel away from the equator, the maximum height of the noon Sun decreases by the same amount.
copy.tl: Sa bawat degree ng latitude na layo mo mula sa equator, ang pinakamataas na taas ng Araw sa tanghali ay bumababa ng parehong halaga.
copy.bis: Sa matag degree sa latitude nga imong palayo sa equator, ang pinakataas nga kataas sa Adlaw sa udto mous-os sa parehas nga kantidad.

copy.en: At solar minimum, the Sun is calm with few sunspots, solar flares, and CMEs! Space weather is quieter for astronauts, but galactic cosmic rays are stronger since the heliosphere is weak.
copy.tl: Sa solar minimum, kalmado ang Sun na may kaunting sunspots, solar flares, at CMEs! Mas payapay ang space weather para sa mga astronaut, pero mas malakas ang galactic cosmic rays dahil mahina ang heliosphere.
copy.bis: Sa solar minimum, kalmado ang Adlaw na adunay gamayng sunspots, solar flares, ug CMEs! Mas malinawon ang space weather para sa mga astronaut, pero mas kusog ang galactic cosmic rays kay huyang ang heliosphere.

copy.en: A sunspot is a dark patch on the Sun caused by strong magnetic forces. It looks dark because it's cooler than the hotter, brighter areas around it!
copy.tl: Ang sunspot ay maitim na batik sa Araw dahil sa malakas na magnetic forces. Mukha itong madilim dahil mas malamig ito kaysa sa mas mainit at maliwanag na paligid!
copy.bis: Ang sunspot usa ka itom nga bahid sa Adlaw tungod sa kusog nga magnetic forces. Murag ngitngit kini tungod kay mas bugnaw kini kaysa sa mas init ug hayag nga palibot!

copy.en: Not all sundials lie flat on the ground! Some are mounted on walls of buildings. These are called vertical sundials, often seen on old churches.
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng sundial ay nakapatag sa lupa! May nakadikit sa pader ng gusali. Tinatawag itong vertical sundials, madalas makita sa lumang simbahan.
copy.bis: Dili tanan sundial patag sa yuta! Ang uban gisumpay sa bongbong sa building. Gitawag kini ug vertical sundials, sagad makita sa daang simbahan.

copy.en:
Why is a soap bubble perfectly spherical?

A sphere has the smallest surface area for the air inside! Surface tension holds the thin soap water film taut, creating beautiful iridescent colours.
copy.tl:
Bakit parang bola ang hugis ng soap bubble?

Ang sphere ay may pinakamaliit na surface area para sa hangin sa loob! Ang surface tension ang nagpapatigas ng manipis na soap water film, kaya nagkakaroon ng magandang kulay.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga spherical ang porma sa soap bubble?

Ang sphere adunay pinakagamayng surface area para sa hangin sulod! Ang surface tension nagpabilin sa manipis nga pelikula sa soapy water nga masikip, nagmugna sa matahum nga iridescent nga mga kolor.
